headline: Voted to explore Evening School Program at 617 Lexington Street and metal detectors, wands at schools; tabled 2025 meeting calendar.
summary: Members heard presentations from the Fine and Performing Arts and Special Education departments, and received enrollment and CTE program updates. They approved the consent agenda and paid bills on warrant. They also voted to explore metal detectors and wands, and to explore a return of the Evening School Program.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda, which included minutes from the September 18, 2024 regular meeting and four resignations. The vote was 'All in favor.'
Approved exploring the implementation of metal detectors and wands at the high school and middle schools. The vote was 'All in favor.'
Tabled the approval of the 2025 School Committee Meeting Calendar. The vote was 'All in favor.'
Approved paying the bills on warrant. The vote was 'All in favor.'
Approved exploring bringing back the Evening School Program and holding it at 617 Lexington Street. The vote was 'All in favor.'

Approved recognizing the National Honor Society students and advisors with a citation from the School Committee for their assistance with the community tours of 554 Lexington Street. The vote was 'All in favor.'

VOTED: On motion of Mr. Frassica, seconded by Mrs. Coleman, to table the approval of the 2025 School Committee Meeting Calendar. All in favor.
VOTED: On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to pay the bills on warrant. All in favor.
VOTED: On motion of Mr. Frassica, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to explore bringing back the Evening School Program and to have it held at 617 Lexington Street. All in favor.

 Stemming from a request at the last meeting, Waltham High’s CTE program 
 enrollment numbers were provided to the members. 
 Dr. Mendonsa shared that representatives from more than sixty colleges and 
 universities were in attendance at the recent college fair held at Waltham High 
 School. 
 Mr. Tarallo asked if CTE courses have a minimum enrollment to run.  A conversation 
 with Mr. Tarallo, Dr. Mendonsa, Mayor McCarthy, and Mrs. AlJammal ensued about 
 program retention, earlier program promotion to students, barriers that may  impact 
 students’ ability to continue in the programs, and a path to college.  The current 
 schedule was noted as a possible deterrent for juniors and seniors as it  typically 
 does not allow for CTE students to take electives and / or AP classes.  Dr. Mendonsa 
 indicated the district just enrolled in a program that will analyze the high school’s 
 schedule for positives and negatives.  She also confirmed administrators will solicit 
 feedback from upperclassmen who left CTE programs. 
 The dates, times and locations for Dr. Mendonsa’s upcoming Community Forums 
 were shared with the Committee. 
 The monthly district enrollment report displayed enrollment at just over 5,600 
 students, which is slightly lower than the original projection. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Frassica, seconded by Mrs.  Coleman, to hear from 
 off-committee members.  All in favor. 
 Fine and Performing Arts Director Blake Siskavich addressed the members and 
 provided a breakdown of the staff’s composition.  He emphasized the program’s 
 focus on integrated learning objectives, student-centered learning and data-driven 
 decisions and also read the department’s shared vision.  Mr. Siskavich highlighted 
 some recent program successes: grants awarded last year, the implementation of the 
 SoundTrap software, the expansion of community partnerships, and the opening of 
 the amazing new high school which will increase opportunities for students.  He also 
 noted a few challenges the department has been facing: the lack of space, 
 particularly at the elementary level, for the increase in instrumental music interest 
 and, as a result, the lack of instrument inventory for students in need.

 Members thanked Mr. Siskavich for his presentation and questions were answered. 
 The positive, long-term benefits of the K-12 drama program were highlighted as being 
 unique for Waltham students. 
 Director of Special Education, Secondary, Alyssa Bourque began with an overview of 
 the 375 staff positions that support the more than 1,000 students on IEPs in the 
 district.  She listed the six specialized SPED programs that are available for WPS 
 students.  Ms. Bourque highlighted the focus areas for this year: specialized new 
 teacher meetings, rollout of the new IEP, quarterly compliance monitoring, a deeper 
 focus on student outcomes, and increasing staff retention from year to year. 
 The director emphasized some big wins and proud moments and also noted some 
 consistent challenges that the department is attempting to tackle. 
 Mr. Zanghi inquired about the AAC iPads and was informed that they have greatly 
 enhanced students’ ability to communicate with others, have expanded learning 
 options and even allow students to track their own progress. 
 Mrs. Coleman asked about special education support at the high school, in 
 comparison to the lower grades.  Ms. Bourque explained the process for parents to 
 follow if they are questioning the services and support being provided within special 
 education. 
 There was nothing new shared in this area. 
 Dr. Mendonsa shared that the first meeting to discuss the upcoming equity audit will 
 be taking place soon. 
 Nothing new relative to the Dual Language School Model was discussed. 
 There was no new information provided. 
 Following the serious incidents at Waltham schools over the last month, a number of 
 parents have asked Mayor McCarthy about metal detectors and wands at the high 
 school and middle schools.  The Mayor confirmed she would like to explore these 
 additional safety measures for our students. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mr.  Frassica, to explore the 
 implementation of metal detectors and wands at the high school and middle schools. 
 All in favor.

 Mayor McCarthy also indicated it is time to re-evaluate whether another campus 
 monitor and / or SRO are needed at Waltham High now that the new school is up and 
 running. 
 A proposed 2025 School Committee Meeting Calendar was provided to the members 
 for review and approval.  Mrs. AlJammal questioned the deviation in the meeting 
 schedule for October, 2025 and Dr. Mendonsa advised the change in schedule is due 
 to a religious holiday. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Frassica, seconded by Mrs.  Coleman, to table the 
 approval of the 2025 School Committee Meeting Calendar.  All in favor. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mrs.  AlJammal, to pay the bills on 
 warrant.  All in favor. 
 Mr. Tarallo asked for the School Committee to have access to the contracts for all 
 staff who are on individual contracts. 
 Mayor McCarthy referenced the former Evening School Program that used to run and 
 noted she would like to explore its return to the district to be located at 617 Lexington 
 Street. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Frassica, seconded by Mrs. AlJammal, to explore bringing 
 back the Evening School Program and to have it held at 617 Lexington Street.  All in 
 favor. 
 The conversation shifted to the WHS NHS students who have been assisting with the 
 community tours of 554 Lexington Street. 
 VOTED:  On motion of Mr. Tarallo, seconded by Mr.  Frassica, to recognize with a 
 citation from the School Committee, the National Honor Society students and

 favor.

 Regular Meeting at 8:20pm. All in favor.
